# A dock Workspace selects its perspective reactively, not by method call

`Scope: high-blast` · `Decision Record: Required: ADR 0029 amend` (§2.1:68 rewritten in place with the old sentence quoted as provenance; §2.1 state-class rows for the intent, the committed name and `pending`; §2.2:211 restated as a collection invariant; the epic's row in the §5 decomposition table) · `Decision Record impact: amends ADR 0029` · graduated from D#18594 (`[GRADUATED_TO_TICKET]` recorded in its body).

## Problem scope

`Neo.tab.Container` selects with `activeIndex_`: a reactive config a provider can bind, a user can write back through `twoWay`, an `activeIndexChange` event, and a split between the public setter (intent) and `_activeIndex` (silent sync from truth). `layout.Card#activeIndex_` and `toolbar.Breadcrumb#activeKey_` are the same idiom. A dock Workspace has an active one-of-N — named perspectives — and selects it by calling a method, then rebuilds its switcher by hand.

The census at `dev@28e56e1543` says why: the dock package carries 35 reactive configs, all on chrome and collaborators (`Rail` 8, `RevealOverlay` 5, `DockSplitter` 4 including `dockZoneDocument_`, `RevealStateMachine` 4, `Preview` 3, `DropIndicators` 3, and one each on `TabContainer`, `Maximize`, `PerspectiveLibrary`, `TopologyLibrary`), while the host `Workspace.mjs` has 3 reactive of ~27 config keys and holds its state in 12 class fields — `dockModel = null` among them. The chrome *receives* the committed document reactively; the host holds it as a field. Header truth became provider data with the header-state work; selection did not. Three consumers therefore hand-roll the same switcher: `examples/dashboard/dock/MainContainer.mjs` (a `layoutCollection` field, `restorePerspective(layoutId)`, and `syncPerspectiveToolbar()` re-run on every re-projection), `examples/dashboard/crossWindow/DemoBWorkspace.mjs` (`collectionChange` → rebuild), and `apps/workstation` (the controller reads `topologyCollection.activeLayoutId` by hand; its topology bar binding the Group provider's history leaves is the precedent this epic generalizes). A fourth consumer family — the Neural Link perspective tools — resolves stored records only and cannot see a declared perspective at all.

**Why an epic.** The shape spans an ADR amendment, the engine host, the model and persistence tiers, three consumers, the Neural Link tool trio across two repositories, and the guides — and the record's own rule (ADR 0029 §5: a leaf that contradicts a section amends the record first, in its own reviewed change) orders those leaves. No single PR can carry it, and the leaves are separable one-PR deliveries with their own falsifiers.

## Intended solution shape

Four parts graduate together; two tiers stay deferred with named triggers. The depth — three divergence matrices, the convergence pass, twelve open questions with dispositions, twelve falsifiers, two receipts at one head — lives in D#18594's body.

1. **Selection — intent config with carried identity.** `perspectives` (initial-only, captured once at construction like `panes` / `zones`; `zones` alone lowers under a reserved name) and `activePerspective_`, the accepted intent: an unknown name is refused by `beforeSetEnumValue`; an accepted name restores through the ordinary commit path; `activePerspectiveChange` fires; a binding may drive it and a user switch may write back. The committed identity is not the config: it travels with the accepted write's descriptor — `{workspaceKey, before, after}`, which the history row already retains — and replay transport hands the direction-appropriate name to `project(context)` on undo and redo. Refusal restores the last committed name under a request serial, never `oldValue`. Under a Group, a restore reconciles panes held by sibling participants: pull home, retire the vessel, or refuse — the leaf chooses and pins it.
2. **Committed truth as provider data, with two writers by boundary.** `dock.perspective.active` and `dock.perspective.modified` publish from the accepted write at the post-commit publication point beside header truth; `modified` uses a declared modification predicate against the selected declared perspective's lowered document (a one-sided edge extent counts; `resizable` is excluded because nothing a user does writes it), and departure stays a separate fact from any unnamed-window count. `dock.perspective.pending` is written by the request lifecycle — start, supersede, refusal, settle — fenced by the request serial, because a held prepare never reaches the post-commit point. The workspace seeds its namespace as an object into whatever provider config it receives, so a consumer formula's first run registers the parent. Reset is its own verb: assigning the current name is a no-op, exactly as in `tab.Container`.
3. **Name sources — one declared list, snapshots beside it.** Selection is declared-only at this stage; saved records are snapshots that may equal but never define a perspective; the reserved name is a write-boundary refusal on both persisted keys; the library's `activeLayoutId` becomes a consumer-owned pointer. Origin metadata follows the accepted-write identity, never the lagging published leaf: a declared-selection append takes its carried after-name, a known-origin hydrate takes the accepted snapshot's declared origin, an originless hydrate or a selection-free write retains the last committed / initialized declared baseline — a history row need not exist, since `preserve` writes return none while the projection context still carries the accepted descriptor. `null` never enters the enum.
4. **The boundary that stays plain.** The six `enableDock*Action` opt-ins remain construction-time (the gate transfers the action's name), `dockActionPolicy` remains the runtime availability seam, and `dockModel` stays a field: the committed document's reactive hook fires inside adoption and on compensation, so publication belongs to the post-commit point, not to a config.

**Deferred with triggers, not in this epic:** the bound catalog (`panes_` under a provider binding, with its queued policy/document/history admission), saved-name selection through the same config (returns with the reservation rule as its constraint), and the committed document as a provider leaf (returns when a consumer must derive its own facts from it, after measuring the deep-equal cost). A per-perspective pane-catalog override — an edge member pinned open in one perspective and auto-hidden in another — is a named trigger for the bound-catalog tier, not a shape this epic's `perspectives` can express: `PerspectiveSelection#capture` lowers every name with the same `panes` catalog, and the zones vocabulary carries no per-item override (surfaced by the Fleet Cockpit's Review preset, which declares a center column instead).

**Leaf shape and order.** Leaves are linked natively to this epic and own their acceptance criteria; the falsifiers F1–F12 from the Discussion are their arms. The ADR amendment lands first by the record's own rule; the selection, published-truth and name-source leaves follow; the consumer deletions (the Workstation one after the topology-bar reset lands, and after the Workstation declares its shipped arrangement — a slice of its own consumer epic), the Neural Link tool trio, the guides and the closure receipt close the set. The Demo B row of the deletion ledger is struck (2026-09-12): Demo B is not an engine `Workspace` host and its four switcher entries are tour-time captures — snapshots, which under E + F stay consumer code; F11's rendered receipt moves to the Workstation leaf. A static-helper reservation gap found in review is its own small leaf. Two standalone core tickets — the `state.Provider` formula gap on absent top-level keys, and a base-class field silently shadowing a subclass reactive config — are referenced, not nested.

## Out of scope

- The bound catalog tier (`panes_` bound to a provider) and its queued policy/document/history contract.
- Saved-name selection through the same config; the committed document as a provider leaf.
- A reactive `dockModel_`; any reactivity for the six `enableDock*Action` opt-ins.
- The Workstation's shipped-baseline readout ("left the shipped arrangement") — a consumer fact with its own baseline, not this epic's `modified`.

## Avoided traps and rejected shapes

- Command-plus-signals with no reactive property (the shipped status quo; `perspectiveLoaded` has zero consumers after a full release).
- Selection as a reducer operation as the identity carrier (the descriptor is already retained; returns only if the accepted-write sequence cannot carry the before-name).
- `dockModel_` as the publication hook (fires inside adoption and on compensation).
- Consumers observing the workspace's configs instead of published data (brings back the sweeps the header-state work deleted).
- A nullable selection for originless snapshots (three special cases the retained baseline makes ordinary).
- Reading `oldValue` on refusal; a silent `_activePerspective` write as the sync mechanism; `modified` folded from the planner's differ without its own predicate; `pending` derived from `refreshPromise`; provenance copied from the published leaf; a blanket underscore conversion of construction-time configs.

### Rationale

Every verdict-blocking condition in §4 is absent. No `BLOCKER`: all 13 subs are closed, and the single `not planned` one was struck in the epic body *before* closure, with public rationale and its criterion re-homed — not abandoned. No untracked `RESIDUAL_L<N>`: each merged PR declares its achieved level against its required level and states `Residual: none`, including the two rows where prose alone would have been insufficient (the guides leaf produced an L3 rendered receipt; the Workstation leaf produced an L3 popup run that CI does not carry). No supersession: the ADR amendment this epic ordered first is live on `dev` and was extended, not replaced, by a later leaf of the same epic.

The deferred tier is the one place a closeout can quietly lose ground, so it is named rather than waved through: the bound catalog (`panes_` under a provider), saved-name selection, and the committed document as a provider leaf carry no tickets **by design** — the epic body defines their return triggers, and a per-perspective pane-catalog override is recorded there as a trigger for the bound-catalog tier rather than a gap in this one. Closing this epic does not convert those into promises anyone is tracking, and it should not.

The `## Unresolved Liveness` section carries forward unchanged and does not bear on this verdict: `gemini` and `kimi` are operator-benched and `@neo-preview` is pending-repoll, which is a graduation-time consensus disposition, not a delivery residual. The epic states it is architecture rather than Tier-2 substrate and therefore carries no `revalidationTrigger` criterion to re-check here.

Per §4, `RECOMMEND_CLOSE_COMPLETED` with zero unresolved residuals makes the close the natural downstream of this review rather than a separate operator gate — explicitly not a §0 Invariant 1 parallel, which governs `gh pr merge` only. Closing on that basis.
